text:
anya: Quick sync — we need to finalize scope boundaries for the Optimize toolkit (batching / caching / quant recommendations + eval-triggered alerts). Customer asks are stacking up; we need a clear MVP. My initial thought: one batching surface (heuristic-driven), KV-prefix caching (in-RAM, persistent opt-in for Dedicated), two quant profiles (safe/aggressive), and a lightweight eval-alert system that posts to Console. Thoughts?

mike: +1 on shipping a minimal surface. Q: do we allow per-request hints in v1 or keep heuristic-only? I vote heuristic-only to avoid API churn.

sam: Heuristic-only is fine for MVP. Ops concern: we need an explicit SLO guard — p95 latency target (hosted) must remain <= 300ms with batching enabled, otherwise we need an automatic bypass.

kevin: For quant recs — propose 2 profiles: `safe` (FP16 + conservative weight quant) and `aggressive` (8-bit weight-only + more ops fused). Each profile must include an expected delta in latency and an estimated quality-risk bucket. Profiles are opt-in per model version. Regression tests required.

lisa: Eval-triggered alerts: trigger when a monitored metric delta > threshold vs baseline (example: rouge/accuracy/embedding-sim). Need per-customer thresholds, noise suppression window, and a sample-extraction for debugging. Who owns eval infra for baselining?

anya: @lisa +1 on thresholds + sampling. We should require a per-customer baseline as part of onboarding. Ops: can we post these alerts to Console notifications? @ops-bot any constraints on schema/rate-limits?

ops-bot: Confirmed. Console can surface alerts. Suggested minimal schema: ```metric, delta_pct, model, model_version, baseline_window_days, sample_ids``` Rate-limit: 1 alert/5m per customer default, configurable. Storage retention: 30 days by default.

mike: KV-prefix caching — should we support persistent disk-backed cache in v1 or start with in-RAM? Persistent reduces cold start but increases infra complexity and cost. Recommend in-RAM first, persisted as opt-in for Dedicated customers.

kevin: Agree with Mike. Start with in-RAM LRU keyed by prefix hash. Offer an explicit `pin` API for Dedicated to persist across restarts in Q2. Also need a metrics dashboard for cache hit/miss and cost delta.

sam: Rollout plan proposal: pilot with 3 customers (diverse workloads), then beta (10 customers), GA. Acceptance criteria: no more than 5% relative drop in customer QA metric after rollout; p95 latency within SLO; and no unexplained increase in cost per token > 10% for hosted.

lisa: One more: for quant recs, include an "explainability" field: short rationale + expected tradeoffs (latency saved, risk level, sample diffs). Customers have asked for this to trust auto-recs.

anya: Action items summary: (1) Product: draft MVP PRD (scope, acceptance criteria, pilot list) — owner @anya. (2) Eng: estimate infra work for batching surface + caching modes + rollout gates — owner @mike. (3) ML: define quant profiles, regression harness, and eval hooks — owner @kevin. (4) Eval/QA: define alert triggers, noise filtering, sampling behavior — owner @lisa. (5) Ops: Console schema and rate-limit integration — owner @ops-bot. Can owners confirm ETAs for initial deliverables?

mike: I'll put infra estimates on my calendar — ETA EOW (7 days).

kevin: ML profiles + baseline regression harness in 2 weeks.

lisa: Eval alert spec + threshold guidance in 10 days.

ops-bot: Console schema + rate-limit implementation plan in 5 business days.

anya: Two tradeoffs to call out explicitly: (A) exclude per-language heuristic tuning from MVP (language-agnostic heuristics only), (B) defer persistent cache as opt-in for Dedicated customers to reduce infra scope. We'll re-evaluate in Q2.

sam: Also flag privacy: for Private deployments, all eval signal processing and alert triggering must be runnable on the customer plane only. Add KMS/HSM and data retention notes in PRD.

kevin: Noted — add encryption at rest for cache + eval samples, and require HSM for signing if customers ask.

anya: Great. I'll draft the PRD with the above constraints and post back here for feedback. If there are no major objections by EOD we'll lock the MVP scope. :rocket: 

mike: acked.

lisa: ack.

sam: ack — adding a quick TODO: include a small telemetry spike detector so we can auto-rollback if we see unexpected regression during canary.

kevin: good call. I'll work with Ops on a rollback hook.

anya: Thanks all — posting PRD soon. If anyone has short examples of metrics to use for the alert baseline, paste them here and I'll fold in.
